html:
The Sukkur Barrage is a great weir across the Indus River at Sukkur in Sindh, built by the British from 1923 to 1932. It feeds one of the largest irrigation systems in the world.

A barrage is a low dam with many gates. It raises the river's level so that water can flow by gravity into canals. Before it, farming in Sindh depended on the Indus flood each summer and on small, unreliable channels. The barrage sent water through seven big canals across millions of acres on both banks, so crops could grow in both seasons.

It turned desert into fields of wheat, cotton and rice, gave Sindh the economic weight to be split off from the Bombay Presidency as its own province in 1936. It followed the model of the Punjab canal colonies upstream.

After 1947 it became a key part of Pakistan's farm economy, and the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 secured its river supply. Silt, aging gates and huge floods, such as the floods of 2010, have strained it.
sum: The Sukkur Barrage is a great weir across the Indus River at Sukkur in Sindh, built by the British from 1923 to 1932. It feeds one of the largest irrigation systems in the world.
